name: Water From Your Eyes
label: Matador
lede: Two Chicago DIY kids who set out to write New Order songs ended up opening for Interpol in front of 160,000 people and cracking Pitchfork's top 20 of 2025.

eras.title: New Order in a Chicago living room
eras.text: Two kids from the Chicago DIY circuit start writing songs together, then move the whole operation to Brooklyn. The first records are small, weird and self-made.

years.src: Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes · Wikipedia: Nate Amos · Wikipedia: Rachel Brown (musician)
years.h: Rachel Brown meets Nate Amos at a house show, and the band starts
years.p: Brown was home from NYU for the summer; Amos was hosting a DIY show at his place in Chicago. Their pitch to each other: write songs like New Order.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the meeting to 2015 and the band's formation to 2016. Brown had been recording alone as thanks for coming since high school, and Amos had been making records as [[This Is Lorelei|a2d140d8-ae17-4d72-b680-b89c77f1ed52]] since around 2013.

Brown's version of the origin, as Wikipedia relays it: "Nate showed me New Order, and we wanted to make New Order kinds of songs." Both later moved to Brooklyn.

years.h: Long Days, No Dreams: the first album, made cheap and fast
years.p: Released in 2017 while Brown was still at NYU. Nothing on it sounds like what came later, which is half the fun of going back.

years.src: Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes discography · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: All a Dance EP arrives on Exploding in Sound
years.p: The first release on the Massachusetts label that would also put out the follow-up, Somebody Else's Song.
years.xp: Wikipedia's discography lists All a Dance as a January 19, 2018 EP on Exploding in Sound. Guitarist and keyboardist Michael Kolb joined the live band in 2018 and stayed until 2022.

eras.title: A record for every lockdown mood
eras.text: The duo keep recording through a pandemic and a breakup, and land on a structure idea borrowed from Scott Walker. Critics start noticing.

years.h: Somebody Else's Song: the first record people wrote about
years.p: Exploding in Sound put it out; reviews singled out the storytelling, the dreamy melodies and Brown's bittersweet delivery.
Recorded and released by the band themselves during the COVID-19 pandemic, and named for its running time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Structure · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Structure puts a breakup on a Scott Walker template
years.p: Eight tracks in two matching halves, with two versions of "Quotations". Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Structure was recorded in 2020 as the romantic relationship between Brown and Amos ended, and that its layout was modeled on Scott Walker's Climate of Hunter. Amos described it as two matching halves with alternating song types.

Pitchfork's Phillipe Roberts called it "cryptic indie pop that hits like a sugar rush"; Paste's Max Freedman gave it 7.8. Later, Brown told The Line of Best Fit the working dynamic got better after the split: "it's so much better because it's way more fun."

eras.title: The longest talking phase
eras.text: Matador courts them for most of a year, then lets them keep every strange thing about the band. The label debut is the record that makes them famous.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: Matador buys the coffee for seven months, then signs them
years.p: Talks began in December 2021 and closed in July 2022, per Brown and Amos in PAPER.
years.xp:
Brown's summary of the courtship: "It's the longest talking phase I've ever experienced." Amos said he arrived with a list of ways to stop the label from changing the band, and never needed it; Matador approved the finished album without notes.

Other labels had asked them to tone the experimental side down. Guitarist and bassist Al Nardo, of [[fantasy of a broken heart|15b40dbf-d08b-49de-8c33-12815c011d7b]], also joined the live band in 2022 as Kolb left.

years.src: Wikipedia: Everyone's Crushed · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Everyone's Crushed: nine songs, 31 minutes, No. 27 of the year
years.p: Pitchfork gave the Matador debut 8.3 and Best New Music, then put it at No. 27 on its 2023 year-end list.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 84 from 14 reviews. Brown told The Line of Best Fit the album was about the American sprawl: strip malls and desolate suburbs standing in for how "Americans failed the American people."

The Guardian called it "the only recent album that sounds the way it does." Rolling Stone ranked it No. 36 and NME No. 28 for 2023.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk
years.h: "Barley" gets picked for an iPhone ad
years.p: PAPER reported the single was chosen for an upcoming Apple iPhone commercial, on the strength of its looped, instantly recognizable sounds.
years.xp: Amos told PAPER he had not thought of "Barley" as a standalone single at all. A live take from July 2023 is on YouTube.

years.h: Crushed by Everyone: the remix album, with a black-metal cold email
years.p: The Dare and Kassie Krut are among the remixers; Amos cold-emailed experimental black metal artist Jute Gyte, whom he had followed for years.

eras.title: Bigger rooms
eras.text: Drummer Bailey Wollowitz makes it a four-piece, and a booking in Mexico City puts them in front of the largest crowd of their lives.

years.src: PAPER: Water From Your Eyes Talk
years.h: Squid tour: Bailey Wollowitz joins on drums for good
years.p: The duo expanded to a four-piece with Wollowitz, of [[fantasy of a broken heart|15b40dbf-d08b-49de-8c33-12815c011d7b]] like Nardo, for the run with UK post-punk band Squid.
years.xp: PAPER reported the February 2024 Squid dates as the point where Wollowitz joined permanently. Wikipedia lists him as a member since 2023.

years.cap: Water From Your Eyes in 2024 · Wikimedia
years.src: Rolling Stone: Interpol in Mexico City · Wikipedia: Water from Your Eyes
years.h: Opening for [[Interpol|b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e]] in Mexico City's Zócalo
years.p: Wikipedia puts the crowd at about 160,000 for the free show, which Rolling Stone called Interpol's biggest ever.
years.xp: Mexican press including Infobae ran explainers on who the American opener was. Wikipedia describes it as the band's largest concert.

years.h: MP3 Player 1: a stopgap EP on Matador
years.p: Released July 12, 2024 between the two big albums.

eras.title: It's a Beautiful Place
eras.text: A quieter, heavier, more existential record wins the best reviews of their career and a spot in Pitchfork's top 20.

years.h: "Life Signs" arrives, with a video Brown directed
years.p: Lead single of It's a Beautiful Place; the video traps the duo in an endless loop of TV shows and commercials.
years.xp: Amos told Nylon the song's guitar part began as a 24-note quarter-tone series generated by a random number generator, then was reworked toward regular rock. Amos produced with audio engineer Howie Weinberg. Rolling Stone's Jon Blistein described the video as the duo "trapped in an endless loop of television."

years.h: "Nights in Armor" is the last single before release
years.p: The third single, released four days ahead of the album, after "Life Signs" (June 4) and "Playing Classics" (July 15).

years.src: Wikipedia: It's a Beautiful Place · Album of the Year: It's A Beautiful Place · NME: It's A Beautiful Place review
years.h: It's a Beautiful Place: Pitchfork's No. 17 album of 2025
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3 and later ranked it No. 17 of the year. Metacritic averaged 82 from 15 critics.
years.xp:
Recorded across 2024 and 2025 mostly in Amos's bedroom and in New York, the ten-track, 29-minute record deals in cosmic insignificance and whether optimism is possible. NME described sci-fi sounds, "frightening existentialism" and a newfound heaviness.

Paste scored it 8.7; Clash, Exclaim! and PopMatters 8. Beyond Pitchfork, it landed at No. 19 on Stereogum's list and No. 55 on Rolling Stone's, and at No. 21 on the UK Independent Albums chart. Album of the Year lists its Pitchfork score as 83.

years.h: First headline tour: North America, then Europe
years.p: The North American run went from September 22 to November 7, with European dates from November 13 to December 7.
A follow-up EP on Matador, released December 3, 2025.
